```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5)
library(lifewatt)
```

This package connects a public facility address to nearby community data. It
supports descriptive exploration; it does not estimate an effect on lifespan.
The installed snapshot works offline.

## Query the Gainesville example

```{r query}
facility <- example_facility()
facility[c("name", "longitude", "latitude", "coordinate_method")]
profile <- nearby_communities(facility$longitude, facility$latitude, radius_km=10)
nrow(profile)
head(profile[c("geoid", "distance_km", "death_rate_per_100k", "small_count")])
```

Distance is measured to the 2020 Census internal point of each tract. A tract
can cross the search circle even if its internal point is inside or outside it.
The facility point is an approximate street-address interpolation.

## View the selected communities

```{r map}
plot_communities(profile)
```

The coloured polygons are selected tracts. Grey background polygons are not
selected; grey selected tracts have small or unavailable death counts. The
star is the query point. Colour indicates the official **crude** all-cause
death rate per 100,000 during 2020-2024, not an AI-related risk score.

## Compare tract distributions

```{r comparisons}
compare_communities(profile)
plot_communities(profile, view="distance")
```

The medians describe an unweighted distribution of tract rates. They are not
pooled death rates for all residents in a band. Rates with fewer than five
reported deaths are excluded by default and counted in `n_excluded`.
Distance bands are descriptive settings, not health-exposure thresholds.

## Keep county life expectancy separate

```{r county}
county_context()
```

This county background value uses a different period and geography. It is not
assigned to tracts. The crude community death rates are not life expectancy.

## Export the rows and reuse the functions

```{r export}
csv <- tempfile(fileext=".csv")
export_communities(profile, csv)
stopifnot(file.exists(csv))
```

The query accepts other coordinates. To explore another county, supply a
compatible `communities` data frame containing unique character GEOIDs,
longitude, latitude, death rates, death counts and a single `health_period`.
Add source and boundary-vintage columns as in `community_data()`. No national
data download is implicit. Custom GEOIDs are plotted as points if bundled
polygons are unavailable.

## Sources and limitations

The inputs come from [Census TIGERweb](https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Census2020/tigerWMS_Census2020/MapServer/6),
[FLHealthCHARTS](https://www.flhealthcharts.gov/ChartsDashboards/rdPage.aspx?rdReport=ChartsMaps.ChartsMapper)
and [UF's HiPerGator history](https://news.ufl.edu/2025/05/the-fourth-generation-model-of-ufs-hipergator/).
The installed `extdata/SOURCES.md` records full provenance and matching rules.
The 2020-2024 window straddles the 2021 AI-system expansion. Age structure,
income, migration, other facilities and spatial dependence are not adjusted.
This single demonstration cannot establish a causal health effect or
represent every commercial AI data center.

Code and documentation were developed with Codex assistance. Team review,
understanding and transparent attribution are required before course use.
